about.title: San Bruno Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a crash takes someone's life on San Bruno roads, the grief is compounded by confusion about what comes next. San Mateo County recorded traffic deaths in recent years, and behind each number is a family left with funeral costs, lost income, and an absence that can't be filled. California law allows a spouse, domestic partner, or children to pursue a wrongful death claim, with certain dependents or heirs able to step in when there's no immediate family. These cases run on a strict two-year clock from the date of death, shorter if a government entity like a city or county road authority is involved. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we simply connect grieving families in San Bruno with an independent attorney who can walk through what happened, explain your options plainly, and handle communications so you have room to grieve. There's no cost to talk, and no fee unless the case recovers something.

whyChoose.title: Why San Bruno Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: We Understand Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to spouses, domestic partners, and children first, with other dependents or heirs eligible in certain cases. We help match your situation with an attorney who can clarify where you stand.

items.title: The Clock Is Real, and Short
items.desc: Wrongful death claims carry a two-year filing deadline from the date of death, and that window shrinks significantly if a government road or agency may be responsible. Reaching out sooner preserves options later.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond the Obvious
items.desc: California law recognizes funeral and burial expenses, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance as compensable losses. An attorney can help identify which losses apply to your family's circumstances.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children have first priority to file. If none exist, certain other dependents or heirs may be eligible depending on the family situation. An independent attorney can review your specific circumstances and explain where you fit.

items.question: How long do we have to file after a death in San Bruno?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim. That period is often shorter if a government entity, such as a city road department, may bear responsibility for a crash on a corridor like El Camino Real or I-380. Waiting can risk losing the ability to pursue a claim at all.

items.question: What if the crash happened during a busy time, like a Friday evening?
items.answer: San Bruno crash records show reported collisions tend to cluster on Fridays between 5 and 7 p.m., often tied to heavier commute traffic. Timing alone doesn't determine fault, but it can help an attorney reconstruct what happened and gather relevant evidence. Every case still depends on its own facts.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to help us?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm, and there's no cost to speak with us. If you're matched with an attorney and they take your case, they work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery.
